amendments.rule: **The 1cs suffix of the divine title `אֲדֹנָי` is lexicalized in the name and takes no English of its own.** In `אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה` → *the Lord Jehovah* the ASV writes no possessive anywhere in the title, so the suffix is its own `unrepresented` unit while `אֲדֹנָ` takes *the Lord*, the supplied *the* joining that noun under rule 15 and the copula of *I am the Lord Jehovah* joining it under rule 20. This is not rule 18: that rule places a suffix the ASV has rendered, and here the ASV has rendered none, so do not reach for a *my* the title does not write. The corpus marks a suffix standing between a `Ncmpc` noun and a proper name `unrepresented` in 250 units across 85 chapters, and aligns `אֲדֹנָ` itself to *the Lord* in 249 units, to *O Lord* in 19, to *of the Lord* in 10 and to *am the Lord* in 4, each time as its own unit. Eleven units in Isaiah instead fuse the pair as one `noncompositional` unit under rule 6; that rule reaches a genuinely indivisible phrase, and rule 2 prefers the split wherever the base noun holds an English word of its own, which in this title it always does. **The order in which the title's two elements stand is no part of the condition.** Where the divine name is written first — `יְהוִה אֲדֹנָי` → *O Jehovah the Lord* — the suffix stands at the end of the title rather than between the construct noun and the name, and nothing changes: the name takes its own English together with any supplied *O* under rule 36, `אֲדֹנָ` takes *the Lord* with the supplied *the* under rule 15, and the suffix is `unrepresented` as before. The corpus signature quoted above describes the commoner order and is not the test; what the test asks is whether the ASV has written a possessive anywhere in the title, which is the subtraction rules 16 and 43 run. **Where the ASV does write a possessive for the suffix, this rule does not reach it.** Outside the fixed title — *O Lord my God*, and the like — rule 18 governs as usual and the suffix takes the word written for it.
amendments.why: PSA.140.7 writes the title in the reversed order `יְהוִה אֲדֹנָי` → *O Jehovah the Lord*, where the 1cs suffix falls at the end of the phrase rather than between a `Ncmpc` noun and a proper name. Rule 57's ground — that the ASV writes no possessive anywhere in the title, so rule 18 has nothing to place — is untouched by element order, but both the rule's example and the corpus signature it quotes describe only the commoner order, so a reader meeting the reversed one could take the rule not to reach it and supply a *my* the ASV never writes. The amendment states that the order is no part of the condition and restates what the test actually asks, leaving the rule's existing corpus counts, its rule 6 carve-out for the Isaiah fusions, and its rule 18 exclusion exactly as they stood. Nothing in the corpus contradicts it: the reversed order recurs in the Psalms, and the ASV renders it with no possessive there as elsewhere.

conventions: Two `אִישׁ` + genitive-of-quality chains stand in this chapter and are analysed two different ways, both times by counting the ASV's words against the morphemes. `אִישׁ חֲמָסִים`/`אִישׁ חָמָס` → *the violent man* (PSA.140.1, 140.4, 140.11) is split under rules 28-29: each noun holds an English word of its own, so the construct takes *man* with the supplied determiner and the rectum takes the attributive *violent*. `אִישׁ לָשׁוֹן` → *An evil speaker* (PSA.140.11) instead fuses under rule 30, because no English word in that rendering is spent on either noun in particular, and the supplied *An* joins the nominal expression under rule 15. What tells the two apart is independently recoverable ownership, not that both are `אִישׁ` chains, and both shapes stand in verse 11.

report: All seven candidate lemmas resolve to context differences the source or the printed ASV licenses, not to one construction analysed two ways. שָׂפָה: v.3 `תַּחַת שְׂפָתֵימוֹ` has no second nominal, so no relational *of*; v.9 `עֲמַל שְׂפָתֵימוֹ` is a construct chain and the rectum takes it under rule 19. לְ before Ncmsc: v.7 `סַכֹּתָה לְרֹאשִׁי` writes the object bare, so the preposition is unrepresented under rule 40, while v.13 writes *unto* for it. חָשַׁב: identical `אֲשֶׁר חָשְׁבוּ` in vv.2 and 4, aligned identically; only the ASV's lexeme and its written auxiliary differ. רֹאשׁ, בְּ, יהוה and הוּא are possessive-vs-supplied-determiner, verb-driven preposition, vocative-vs-subject, and possessive-vs-object.

The chapter holds rule 44's preposition boundary consistently in both directions: v.6 `הַאֲזִינָה ... קוֹל` has no preposition morpheme, so the supplied *unto* joins the verb, while v.13 `יוֹדוּ לִשְׁמֶךָ` gives *unto* to the written לְ. Same count, opposite outcomes, both correct.

The refrain `אִישׁ חֲמָסִים`/`אִישׁ חָמָס` → *the violent man* stands in vv.1, 4 and 11 and is split identically in all three: the construct noun takes its own *man* with the determiner rule 29 supplies, the rectum takes the attributive *violent*. `אָדָם רָע` → *the evil man* in v.1 reaches the same English head noun by rule 15 rather than rule 29, which is right for a noun with an absolute adjective rather than a construct chain.

The five `added` units, which the lemma table cannot see, were each read against the morphemes standing in their own clause: *lest* (v.8) and *whence* (v.10) over clauses with no subordinator or relative morpheme in them (rule 55, with rule 46 excluding a clause juxtaposed to a written antecedent), *As for* (v.9) before a fronted phrase carrying no marker and no preposition (rule 16's limit), *And* (v.12) for a colon with no waw (rule 14's closing sentences), *their* (v.2) for a phrase with no suffix (rule 18's closing sentence). Nothing is marked `added` in one verse and folded into a licensing morpheme in another: the waw of v.5 takes its written *and*, and every supplied determiner in vv.4-13 goes to a morpheme that licenses it.

Both rule 30 fusions — `יַד־מַעְגָּל` → *wayside* (v.5) and `כָּל־יוֹם` → *Continually* (v.2) — head on the governing construct under rule 23's tie sentence. `אִישׁ לָשׁוֹן` → *An evil speaker* (v.11) fuses on the same terms while `אִישׁ חָמָס`, two words later in that verse, splits, because there the ASV spends a word on each morpheme. That contrast is recorded as a convention.

BSB disagreements: none is an error, and no accepted edge was moved to change the 98.0%. The `Sh` paragogic he of `הַאֲזִינָה` (v.6) is rule 32, which names these as the bulk of the BSB disagreements in the Psalms; the 1cs suffix of `אֲדֹנָי` (v.7) is rule 57; the לְ of `לְרֹאשִׁי` (v.7) is rule 40, the recasting BSB attaches to its phrase. All three are documented convention differences.

Verses 0 and 1-13 are all present and the ASV/WLC superscription offset is already resolved in the packet, so rule 54 does not arise. The two selected variant units (vv.10, 12) and the one underdetermined unit (v.9) are all resolved to the base reading in the projection, and none of them carries the FALLBACK EXCLUDED BY EVIDENCE mark, so rule 53 does not arise either.
